United KingdomUnited StatesDeutschlandFranceEspañaItaliaInternationalSelect a countryUnited KingdomUnited StatesDeutschlandFranceEspañaItaliaInternationalMenuPublic dataSolutionsCompanyPanelist supportContact salesSearchLog inSign upVoting intention, 11-12 October 2026: Lab 24%, Con 23%, Ref 21%, LD 12%, Grn 11%YouGov -13 October 2026Latest YouGov Westminster voting intention figuresThe latest YouGov voting intention poll for The Times and Sky News shows a close race between the largest parties, with Labour, the Conservatives and Reform UK all within the margin of error of each other.

Our latest figures show Labour on 24% of the vote, down three points on last week’s poll, while the Conservatives are up three points to 23%, their highest level since we restarted our voting intention tracker in January 2025. Reform UK take a 21% share in this week’s poll, their joint-lowest on our tracker this parliament.

The Lib Dems are on 12% of the vote and the Greens are on 11%, both within the margin of error of our previous poll.

Although Labour’s figure is down on last week, it is still above any figure recorded for the party in our tracker during the final twelve months of Keir Starmer’s leadership. Additionally, for both Labour and the Conservatives, this marks a substantial recovery since early May, when the combined vote share of the two historic parties stood at just 33%, relative to 47% in our latest figures.

Read about our voting intention methodology here
